newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will head a panel to investigate land grab claims in Nakhon Ratchasima province including the allegation that his wife has acquired land there. General Chavalit has vowed to be relentless in his fact-finding mission, saying he will disprove any allegations made by the newspapers and the opposition. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Prospects of the draft constitution being passed into law have dimmed, with the government distancing itself from the political reform process. The prime minister, who pledged to support political reform, says the government can not be held responsible for the success or failure of the charter draft. Coalition parties will be given a free vote on the draft. (BANGKOK POST)

- The government has deferred plans to privatise the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand after strong protests from workers. Under an agreement reached between Prime Minister's Office Minister Rakkiat Sukthana, EGAT Governor Preecha Chungwattana and Employees' Association president, any plan to allow private firms to take up power generation work from the agencies will be suspended. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Cabinet has approved a series of tax relaxation measures, including a Finance Ministry proposal to waive value-added tax (VAT) for air and marine cargo companies. The intention of exempting the cargo transport industry from VAT is to create a fairer competitive environment for the industry. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Eastern Seaboard development committee has approved an initial budget of 600 million baht to fund the first year of construction of the Asia Global TransPark at U Ta-pao in Chon Buri province. The committee also expresses support for measures aimed at cutting customs delays and liberalising air traffic regulations at the facility. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Transport and Communications Ministry will not confirm if the Telecom Master Plan will be submitted to Cabinet this month as scheduled, but is insisting the proposed privatisation of the Telephone Organisation of Thailand must come first. This new priority arrangement raises the possibility that the telecom industry may have to do without a master plan. (THE NATION)
